title: Palestinian Nakba
summary: In 1948, around the first Arab-Israeli war, an estimated 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled from their homes, according to EBSCO; the scholar Darweish writes of about 750,000. Palestinians call these events the Nakba, or catastrophe. Accounts of cause differ: some Jewish leaders cited Arab broadcasts, while historians point to flight or expulsion. UN General Assembly Resolution 194 followed in December 1948.

uncertainty.note: Year only; the sources tie the events to the war that followed May 1948.

as_recorded.value: displacement, and dispossession experienced by Palestinians in 1948 would become known as the Nakba

where.modern_name: Former Mandatory Palestine (Israel and the Palestinian territories); pin at Jerusalem

importance.justification: Displacement of several hundred thousand Palestinians in 1948 that shaped the later refugee question and Palestinian national memory.

audience_note: This record concerns mass displacement and violence in a conflict that remains politically contested. Figures and causes are attributed to their sources; Palestinian and Israeli accounts differ on cause and terminology.
